title: Normal integral geometry core
statement: Let S be an integral scheme whose local rings are integrally closed, and let c:C → S be smooth with geometrically connected fibres and C nonempty [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, def-sbc-normal-dominant-galois, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Let q:Cη → Spec K(S), j:Cη → C form the cartesian generic fibre [def-pc-fibre-product]. Then C and Cη are integral, and every local ring of either scheme is integrally closed. No Noetherian, quasi-compactness or separatedness hypothesis is required.

proof.text: Smoothness preserves normal local rings (034F). Openness (01UA) and C nonempty imply that the generic fibre is nonempty. Smooth base change and geometric connectedness make Cη a connected smooth scheme over K(S). It is locally noetherian and normal (056T); its irreducible components are disjoint and open, so connectedness gives integrality. Every nonempty open of C has open image containing the generic point of S and hence meets j(Cη). The dense image of the irreducible Cη makes C irreducible, and its normal stalks make it reduced. Thus C is integral and both schemes have integrally closed local rings. This is the remaining unformalized geometric argument, detailed in the theorem docstring.

lean.statement:
theorem smooth_connected_generic_geometry_core {S C : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral S]
    [Nonempty C] (hS : ∀ x : S, IsIntegrallyClosed (S.presheaf.stalk x))
    (c : C ⟶ S) [Smooth c] [GeometricallyConnected c]
    {Cη : Scheme.{u}} (q : Cη ⟶ Spec S.functionField) (j : Cη ⟶ C)
    (hCη : IsPullback q j (S.fromSpecStalk (genericPoint S)) c) :
    ∃ hC : IsIntegral C, letI := hC;
      ∃ hη : IsIntegral Cη, letI := hη;
        (∀ x : C, IsIntegrallyClosed (C.presheaf.stalk x)) ∧
        (∀ x : Cη, IsIntegrallyClosed (Cη.presheaf.stalk x))
